name: Shiv Nadar
title: The Rooftop Dreamer Who Gave It Back
subtitle: A Tamil village, a rooftop room in Delhi, a bet on the microchip, and then one of India's biggest giving stories: how Shiv Nadar built HCL and handed it on.
hook: Shiv Nadar was schooled mainly in Tamil and ==did not start speaking much English until he was 22==. Yet the company he co-founded in a rooftop room in Delhi in 1976 now employs **more than 230,000 people in 60 countries**. And on the 2025 EdelGive Hurun list, he and his family gave away ₹2,708 crore, about ==₹7.4 crore a day==.

glance.label: Born
glance.value: 14 July 1945, in Moolaipozhi village, in what is now Thoothukudi district, Tamil Nadu

glance.label: Grew up
glance.value: Small-town Tamil Nadu. He went to school in Kumbakonam and Madurai, mostly in Tamil, and first saw a big city, Chennai, at 21

glance.label: Education
glance.value: Electrical and electronics engineering at PSG College of Technology, Coimbatore, on a full scholarship he credits with making HCL possible

glance.label: First job
glance.value: Management trainee at DCM in Delhi, according to his university's biography; he joined DCM's textile arm in 1968 and by 1971 ran sales and marketing at its new electronics unit

glance.label: First company
glance.value: Microcomp, which sold calculators, then Hindustan Computers Ltd (HCL), founded on 11 August 1976 in a rooftop room in Delhi, when he was about 31

glance.label: Main company today
glance.value: HCLTech: over 230,000 people in 60 countries and $14.8 billion revenue in the 12 months to September 2026. He is Chairman Emeritus and Strategic Advisor to the Board

glance.label: Source of wealth
glance.value: Software services, self-made. Forbes: about $31.4 billion (#71) on 1 November 2026. Bloomberg: $36.7 billion (#61) on 31 October 2026

glance.label: Family
glance.value: Married to Kiran Nadar, art collector and Asian Games bridge medallist. One daughter, Roshni Nadar Malhotra, who has chaired HCLTech since July 2020 and received his 47% holding-company stakes as gifts in March 2025

glance.label: Known for
glance.value: Co-founding HCL, and giving: ₹2,708 crore with his family on the 2025 Hurun list, and over US$1.85 billion invested through the Shiv Nadar Foundation he set up in 1994

contact.howToReach: Shiv Nadar has no public personal email that we could find, and we found no verified personal social account, so treat any profile in his name with suspicion and never guess an address. He has also stepped back from running HCLTech: he is Chairman Emeritus and Strategic Advisor, and his daughter Roshni chairs the company and now controls the family holding companies, so a letter addressed to him personally is the weakest route. Pick the door that fits your reason: education ideas go to the Shiv Nadar Foundation, rural students to VidyaGyan, shareholders to investors@hcltech.com, journalists to the HCLTech newsroom contacts, and business proposals to the HCLTech or HCL Group contact forms. Climate founders should also watch the HCL Group website, which has announced a ClimaForce Fund for climate innovators. Keep your message to five lines: who you are, the one thing you want, why it fits that organisation, and one link.

factCheck.method: Contact details and socials were read from each organisation's own pages. Biography facts were read from Forbes, Bloomberg, stock-exchange filings, HCL and foundation pages, and established press. Photos and licences come from the Wikimedia Commons API, and each photo was viewed before use. Files tagged GODL-India were left out because that licence is not on this book's allowed list. Reading was limited by a shared search budget that ran out mid-task and by sites that refused automated reading, including Mint, The Hindu and Business Standard.

disputed.note: Forbes says he and five friends. Rediff says five colleagues and OneIndia names six engineers in all. Fortune India and Voice&Data say he left with seven colleagues, Outlook says eight young men quit, and DQ Channels says about ten colleagues. Wikipedia lists eight names. The counts may reflect different moments. We avoid giving one number here.

disputed.claim: How much money HCL started with
disputed.note: OneIndia says the founders pooled ₹1.87 lakh. Rediff and Business Today give about ₹20 lakh, with Business Today saying it was earned from selling calculators. Voice&Data prints a garbled 2 million with no clear currency. Gulf Business, seen in search results only, gives $2,300. The smaller figure may be the first pooled money and the larger one the sum that funded HCL, but we could not confirm that. We avoid giving one number here.

His university's biography says his career started as a DCM management trainee, and DQ Channels dates his joining DCM to 1968. Wikipedia, citing Harish Damodaran's book India's New Capitalists (2008), says he first worked at Cooper Engineering, a Walchand group company in Pune, in 1967. We could not read the book directly, so the glance uses DCM.

disputed.claim: His age when he took the DCM electronics job
disputed.note: DQ Channels says he was 23 in 1971. A 1945 birth would make him about 26, so we left the age out.
Outlook confirms 1945 and Forbes lists him as 81 in November 2026, which fits. The exact day, 14 July, comes from Wikipedia citing Sharma's 2003 reference book, and we did not find it in a filing.

disputed.claim: The age at which he started speaking much English
disputed.note: Forbes says 22. Lower-quality biography sites say 21 or 22. We use Forbes.
Forbes shows $31.4 billion (#71) on 1 November 2026, and Bloomberg shows $36.7 billion (#61) on 31 October 2026. Both are live estimates with different methods, so we show both.

disputed.claim: How much he has put into the Foundation
disputed.note: Forbes and Fortune India say $1.1 billion, his university page says $1.5 billion as of June 2024, and the Foundation's homepage says over $1.85 billion. These look like figures from different dates. The glance uses the Foundation's own latest figure.

disputed.claim: HCL's 1978 computer as a world first
disputed.note: HCL Group says it introduced an 8-bit microprocessor-based computer in 1978 well before its global peers, and Outlook calls it a world first. Other 8-bit microcomputers, such as the Apple II from 1977, were already on sale, so we do not state this as a world first.

A text extraction of the March 2025 filing reads New Delhi 110009, while the BSE shareholder notice, seen as a search excerpt because the PDF refused direct reading, reads 110 019. We use 110019, the PIN the BSE notice gives. A reader sending post should confirm it on a current filing.

Fortune India says he lost his father early and grew up with financial hardship. Lower-quality biography sites call the father a lawyer or a district judge. We could not settle this from a reliable source, so the glance leaves it out.
